common_calibration.description: Scores recomputed from the six verified pickle inputs; fixed-seeded exact-pivot-null calibration with randomized cutoff boundaries; the same cutoff is used on the released raw and watermarked documents.

alternative_prior.scope: Bayesian methods in the released-output analysis

tail_width.atoms: dyadic ladder 1, 4, 16, ... strictly below V-1 on the released vocabulary; see bayes_uniontail.by_model
tail_width.scope: width branch of the Gumbel union-tail rows

bayes_uniontail.hierarchy_scope: This records the hierarchies evaluated, not a general claim that tokenwise mixtures cannot improve power.
bayes_uniontail.why_gumbel_only: The working inverse limiting alternative depends on Delta alone.
bayes_uniontail.component: A union of a full-width Dirichlet tail-shape branch and an equal-weight live-tail-width branch restricted to J < V-1. The width component is f_{Delta,J}(r) = r**(Delta/(1-Delta)) + J*r**(J/Delta-1). The shape component uses the tabulated psi_alpha transform.

tail_width_prior.family: uniform on the configured ladder strictly below V-1
tail_width_prior.note: The equal-tail atom (alpha=inf, J=V-1) belongs to the shape branch. It is excluded from the width branch to avoid counting the full-width atom twice.

normalisation.note: Both branches integrate to one analytically. The width formula is closed form; the shape implementation interpolates a transform table. Tokenwise scoring, when requested, also uses outer lookups. Numerical mass and node-sensitivity checks are not certificates that the evaluated densities have mass at most one. The exact test-martingale result requires conditional null validity and analytic or certified normalized evaluation; it is not asserted for these interpolated implementations.

primary.name: formal_eta_j_over_v_minus_1
primary.watermarked_reconstruction: recover rank = round(eta_stored*(V-1)+1), validate its integer residual, then abs(float64(U_float32)-rank/(V-1))

sensitivity.name: upstream_shifted_eta_j_minus_1_over_v_minus_1
sensitivity.score_definition: apply the primary score formulas to shifted pivots and recalibrate each score on simulated shifted-null paths
sensitivity.status: coordinate sensitivity only; not interpreted as a Bayes factor under the shifted pivot law

output_schema.rows: one sample x method x horizon record

seed_context_reuse.interpretation: repeated context tokens address repeated PRF seeds under the released skipgram implementation
repeated context tokens address repeated PRF seeds under the released skipgram implementation

torch_uses: replay the released CPU fixed-table hash and seeded PRF draws

trgof.accumulation: the statistic sorts the p-values of the whole prefix, so it is recomputed from scratch at every reported horizon; no cumulative sum exists for it
trgof.atom_at_zero: rows whose truncated index set is empty score exactly zero, so the statistic has an atom; the randomized-boundary treatment already applied to every rule covers it, and n_at_boundary is reported per row
trgof.calibration: routed through the shared calibration path: the same common exact pivot-null sample, the same nominal level, and the same randomized score=c boundary rule as every other rule

gumbel_p_value.status: the authors' definition, exactly as released

trgof.implementation: code/trgof.py, the single owner of the statistic in this study, asserted term for term against the released code

inverse_p_value.definition: p = F_0(d), the exact finite-vocabulary null CDF of d = |U - eta(I)|
inverse_p_value.shifted_convention_treatment: the shifted sensitivity applies the same p-value map to shifted pivots and recalibrates on the simulated shifted-null sample, exactly as every other inverse score is treated under that convention
inverse_p_value.status: OUR EXTENSION, not the authors'.  Their released code applies Tr-GoF to Gumbel-max pivots only and defines no p-value for the inverse-transform pivot.  Small d is the evidence direction there, so the one-sided p-value is the null CDF rather than its complement; the exact finite-vocabulary CDF keeps it uniform under the null.
inverse_p_value.vocabulary_source: the released vocabulary of each model, carried through ReleasedModelData and cross-checked against the released eta tensors by the integer-rank reconstruction; no vocabulary size is hardcoded in the Tr-GoF path

trgof.label: Tr-GoF, s=2 (HC)
trgof.randomness_note: the rule reads the pivot arrays already scored by every other detector and touches no generator, so all pre-existing records are bit-identical with and without it
trgof.reference: Tr-GoF of Li, Ruan, Wang, Long and Su (2026; preprint 2024); released implementation github.com/lx10077/TrGoF, compute_score
trgof.sensitivity_note: the authors' simulation code sweeps s over [2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.5, 0.0]; only s = 2, the Higher Criticism member their figures lead with, is carried as a rule, because the released-output tables are already large.  The other indices are available from trgof.DEFAULT_S_VALUES and change no other rule.
trgof.statistic: S_n(s) = n * max_t K_s(t/n, p_(t)) over the truncated one-sided index set p_(t) >= 1/n and t/n >= p_(t)

generation_design.document_selection: first 500 stream records with sufficient tokenized length; no shuffle
generation_design.raw_temperature_note: the released raw-generation function does not apply the command-line temperature, so it samples from unscaled logits

upstream.provenance_limit: the released tensors are commit-pinned, but the model and C4 revisions used to generate them were not recorded upstream

upstream_recorded.description: Stored rejection-rate arrays read verbatim from the eight commit-pinned JSON files; result-array power is converted to Type-II error as one minus the stored rate.
upstream_recorded.inverse_cutoff_caveat: The inverse optimal-score cutoff simulations are unseeded and are rerun separately in the upstream null and watermarked calls. For 2p7B, each horizon uses the pointwise minimum of 13 simulated cutoff curves. The upstream inverse pivots also use the shifted (rank-1)/(V-1) convention.

comparison.mcse_warning: The two rates use the same 500 released documents, but the upstream JSON contains only aggregate rates. Their covariance and a paired MCSE for the difference therefore cannot be recovered from these files. The marginal MCSEs are reported separately.

curve_schema.error_rate: rejection_rate for released raw documents; 1-rejection_rate for released watermarked documents
curve_schema.mcse: sample standard deviation divided by sqrt(500); upstream binary rates are reconstructed from their exact multiples of 1/500

figure_policy.type_i_axis_scale: symlog with linear threshold .01, retaining the discrete short-prefix spikes at n=1 without compressing values near .05
figure_policy.upstream_unplotted_methods: The additional pinned upstream reference-score curves remain in the CSV; the figure uses the overlapping displayed menu to keep its 4-by-2 panels legible.

interpretation_limits: The two analyses are not Monte Carlo replicates of one fixed test because their cutoff constructions differ.
The same 500 documents underlie both sets of rates, but the upstream JSON files do not retain per-document decisions; a paired MCSE for their difference is therefore unavailable.
The released watermarked continuations end at 200 scored tokens, so these files cannot support matched power curves beyond n=200.
